_note: `ref="name"` — the universal attribute that publishes an element's backing platform view into the shared-handle registry so a MODULE can reach it (Core/Capture's element/pdf, <scroll>.toElement, <Spotlight>'s target rect). The whole point is that the kernel names no consumer: it publishes under a derived key and any module resolves it through the bus. keys[] pins the derivation — trimmed, exact case, prefixed `ref.` so a ref can never collide with a first-class handle like `web` or `view`; a whitespace-only name is NO ref rather than a handle named the empty string, which would be a registry slot every anonymous element fought over. lifecycle[] pins provide-on-appear / clear-on-disappear and the two cases that make the typed absence honest: a name nothing ever published (`unknown_ref`) versus a name that WAS published and whose view has gone (also `unknown_ref`, because the registry holds handles WEAKLY and a dead view must not read as a live one). reuse[] pins the case a recycled list row creates: the same name re-provided replaces, and the LAST provider wins, so a scrolled-away row cannot keep ownership of a ref a visible row now claims.

keys.name: inner spaces survive (a name is opaque)
a dotted name is not a chain, just a name
a name may not shadow a first-class handle, because it is namespaced

lifecycle.name: resolving a name that never appeared is unknown_ref
a collected view reads as unknown_ref, never as a live handle
clearing one name leaves the other

reuse.name: re-providing the same name replaces, and the last provider wins
a recycled row that disappears AFTER a new one claimed the name does not clear it
reuse._note: The list-recycling order: the incoming row mounts before the outgoing row unmounts. A naive clear-on-disappear would leave the visible row's ref dead.

reuse.name: the current provider disappearing does clear it
